interactions.summary: A student rejects determinism on Dante's behalf, another offers a God-as-AI foreknowledge model, and Jiang keeps the pressure on by insisting that contribution to the plan still leaves a moral problem unresolved.

speaker_notes.note: The repaired transcript includes a brief `UNKNOWN` filler acknowledgment that does not carry substantive content.

claims.claim: A student says Dante cannot be a determinist because free will has been treated as a fundamental principle throughout the course, and Jiang agrees.
A student proposes an AI-like foreknowledge model in which God sees the outcome of human choices and prepares responses without directly causing those choices.
Jiang grants the AI-like explanation as intelligible but stresses that it does not dissolve the problem that traitors still contribute to the divine plan.
Another student drifts toward a Matrix-like or psychedelic-perception frame in which creation is a staged experience meant to affect consciousness, not straightforward reality.

signature_moments.moment: God is analogized to AI or AlphaGo: not forcing your move, but foreseeing the board and preparing countermoves in advance.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's most contemporary compression of the providence-versus-free-will problem.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The rejected option that would make Dante's universe run on fixed outcomes rather than meaningful free will.

chronology_notes.note: The class explicitly rules out strict determinism and experiments with foreknowledge models instead, but Jiang still treats the moral status of providential betrayal as unsolved.

uncertainty_notes.note: The students explicitly mark these models as speculation rather than settled doctrine.
